title: The riddle keeper's dice
concept: random · seed, randint, choice and shuffle
description: Roll the riddle keeper's dice, and learn why a seed makes chance repeatable.

tasks.title: Numbers you cannot guess
tasks.body: import random gives a program chance. random.randint(1, 6) picks a whole number from 1 to 6, both included. random.choice(paths) picks one item from a list, and random.shuffle(cards) mixes a list in place.
tasks.detail: The numbers only look random: they are worked out from a starting number called a seed. random.seed(7) at the start makes every run give the same numbers, which is how games are tested and how this page checks your program. Without a seed, each run differs.

tasks.code:
# The same seed gives the same "random" story every time
import random
random.seed(7)
print(random.randint(1, 6))
print(random.choice(["left", "right", "up"]))
cards = ["sun", "moon", "star"]
random.shuffle(cards)
print(cards)
tasks.note: With the seed set to 7, these three lines come out the same on every run, on any computer with the same Python.

tasks.question: If the program ran again with the same seed, what would it print?
tasks.why: A seed fixes where the numbers start, so the same seed gives the same numbers in the same order.

tasks.prompt: Predict, then run it twice: the same lines both times. Then take out random.seed(7) and run it a few times.

The riddle keeper rolls dice. Ask for the number of dice and the number of sides each one has. Roll every die with random.randint(), from 1 to the number of sides, and print each roll on its own line, then the total of all the rolls on the last line. Do not call random.seed() yourself: the check sets the seed, so its numbers match yours.
tasks.starter: # Import random, then roll each die
hints: Import random at the top. A for loop over range() rolls once per die.
Each roll is random.randint(1, sides): store it, print it, and add it to a total that starts at 0 before the loop.
With other names: coin = random.randint(0, 1) flips a coin, and heads = heads + coin counts the heads.

error_hints.text: random is a name only after import random, at the top of the program.
randint() and range() need whole numbers: turn each reply into one with int(...).
If your rolls differ from the ones shown, check that you did not call random.seed() yourself, and that each die is rolled once, with randint(1, sides), in order.
A die with 20 sides rolls from 1 to 20: the second number in randint() is the number of sides.
With three two-sided dice, each roll is 1 or 2, and the last line adds them up.
Check many dice: one roll per die, and the total of them all at the end.
Check a die with only one side: it always rolls 1.

similar_example.code:
import random
random.seed(1)
heads = 0
for flip in range(4):
    coin = random.randint(0, 1)
    heads = heads + coin
print(heads)
similar_example.note: Four coin flips with a fixed seed, counting heads. Your dice print every roll as well as the total.

other_ways.code:
from random import randint
dice = int(input("Dice? "))
sides = int(input("Sides? "))
rolls = []
for n in range(dice):
    rolls.append(randint(1, sides))
for roll in rolls:
    print(roll)
print(sum(rolls))
other_ways.note: Keep the rolls in a list first, then print them and add them up with sum().

other_ways.code:
import random
dice = int(input("Dice? "))
sides = int(input("Sides? "))
total = 0
while dice > 0:
    roll = random.randrange(1, sides + 1)
    print(roll)
    total += roll
    dice -= 1
print(total)
other_ways.note: randrange() stops just before its second number, so randrange(1, sides + 1) picks from the same numbers as randint(1, sides), and gives the same rolls.
